name: Gallio
title: The Proconsul of Achaia
summary: Gallio was the Roman proconsul in the province of Achaia (Greece) around the year 51–52 AD. He is known from the Bible for rejecting the Jews' accusations against the apostle Paul in Corinth and refusing to intervene in what he considered an internal religious dispute. His decision had significant importance for the early Christian mission, as it effectively allowed Paul to continue his preaching.

keyEvents.title: The Jews Bring Paul Before Gallio
keyEvents.description: The Jews in Corinth brought Paul before the proconsul's court and accused him of persuading people to worship God contrary to the law.

keyEvents.title: Gallio Rejects the Accusation
keyEvents.description: Gallio rejected the charges, stating that if it concerned words and names and the Jews' own law, he would not judge such matters. He regarded it as an internal religious dispute, not a criminal case.

keyEvents.title: Gallio Drives Them Away from the Court
keyEvents.description: Gallio drove them all away from the court and refused to get further involved in the matter, which effectively acquitted Paul.

keyEvents.title: Sosthenes is beaten before the court
keyEvents.description: After Gallio dismissed the case, the crowd seized Sosthenes, the synagogue ruler, and beat him in front of the court, but Gallio did not care about this.

keyEvents.title: Paul remains in Corinth
keyEvents.description: Thanks to Gallio's decision, Paul was able to stay in Corinth and preach the gospel without legal persecution for a longer period.
